events.title: .NET 4.5 and C# 5.0 with async/await released
events.summary: Microsoft shipped .NET Framework 4.5 on August 15, 2012 with C# 5.0 `async` and `await` — bringing asynchronous programming into mainstream .NET.
events.about: C# 5's async model let [UI] and server code read linearly while awaiting I/O: `await client.GetAsync(url)` without callback pyramids. It shaped ASP.NET Web [API], WPF apps, and later patterns across the .NET ecosystem before minimal APIs and channels.

narrative.whyChosen: Async/await in C# 5 changed how .NET developers wrote responsive servers and desktop apps.
narrative.whyImportant: The compiler transformed async methods into state machines — a model later copied across languages.
narrative.problemSolved: BeginInvoke, callbacks, and `Task.ContinueWith` made asynchronous .NET code hard to read and maintain.

events.title: Shopware 4 open sourced
events.summary: Shopware released version 4.0 on August 28, 2012 under the AGPL license — making the e-commerce platform officially open source.
events.about: Shopware 4 disclosed its full PHP codebase — themes under Apache 2.0 — after years of a paid Community Edition preview. The move accelerated adoption across Europe and established Shopware as [Magento]'s main open-source rival in the DACH market.

narrative.whyChosen: Shopware 4's AGPL release committed the platform to open-source e-commerce.
narrative.whyImportant: It expanded the European open-source commerce ecosystem beyond [Magento].
narrative.problemSolved: Merchants wanted inspectable, extensible cart software without proprietary lock-in.

events.title: Zoom first public beta ships
events.summary: Eric Yuan's team shipped Zoom's first public beta on August 21, 2012 — a cloud video meeting platform built by former WebEx engineers.
events.about: Zoom prioritized one-click joins and reliable screen share over enterprise telepresence complexity. Developers adopted it for standups, pair programming, and remote interviews long before COVID — then usage exploded in 2020 when offices closed. Its [API] and [SDK] powered embedded video in education and health apps.

narrative.whyChosen: Zoom became the default video layer for remote engineering teams.
narrative.whyImportant: Frictionless meetings made distributed standups and interviews routine.
narrative.problemSolved: Legacy WebEx and Skype calls were painful to join and dropped constantly.
